passages.text: King Nebuchadnezzar, To the people of every nation and language who dwell in all the earth: May your prosperity be multiplied.
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar speaks.
He is the king of Babylon.
He addresses all people.
He speaks to every nation.
He speaks to every language group.
He speaks to everyone who lives on the earth.
He wishes them prosperity.
He says, “May your prosperity increase.”
passages.original: נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֣ר מַלְכָּ֗א לְֽכָל־ עַֽמְמַיָּ֞א אֻמַיָּ֧א וְלִשָּׁנַיָּ֛א דִּֽי־ דָאֲרִין בְּכָל־ אַרְעָ֖א שְׁלָמְכ֥וֹן יִשְׂגֵּֽא׃

passages.text: I am pleased to declare the signs and wonders that the Most High God has performed for me.
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar speaks.
He addresses all people of every nation and language on earth.
He says he is pleased.
He wants to declare what God has done.
The Most High God has performed signs for him.
The Most High God has performed wonders for him.
He wants everyone to know about these acts.
passages.original: אָֽתַיָּא֙ וְתִמְהַיָּ֔א דִּ֚י עֲבַ֣ד עִמִּ֔י אֱלָהָ֖א עִלָּיָא שְׁפַ֥ר קָֽדָמַ֖י לְהַחֲוָיָֽה׃

passages.text: How great are His signs, how mighty His wonders! His kingdom is an eternal kingdom; His dominion endures from generation to generation.
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar speaks.
He describes the Most High God.
God’s signs are great.
God’s wonders are mighty.
God’s kingdom lasts forever.
God’s rule continues through every generation.
passages.original: אָת֙וֹהִי֙ כְּמָ֣ה רַבְרְבִ֔ין וְתִמְה֖וֹהִי כְּמָ֣ה תַקִּיפִ֑ין מַלְכוּתֵהּ֙ מַלְכ֣וּת עָלַ֔ם וְשָׁלְטָנֵ֖הּ עִם־ דָּ֥ר וְדָֽר׃

passages.text: I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at ease in my house and flourishing in my palace.
passages.sermon:
I am Nebuchadnezzar.
I am the king of Babylon.
I felt safe in my house.
I prospered in my palace.
passages.original: אֲנָ֣ה נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֗ר שְׁלֵ֤ה הֲוֵית֙ בְּבֵיתִ֔י וְרַעְנַ֖ן בְּהֵיכְלִֽי׃

passages.text: I had a dream, and it frightened me; while in my bed, the images and visions in my mind alarmed me.
passages.sermon:
Nebuchadnezzar was the king of Babylon.
He had a dream.
This dream frightened him.
He was lying in his bed.
He saw images in his mind.
He saw visions in his mind.
These images and visions alarmed him.
passages.original: חֵ֥לֶם חֲזֵ֖ית וִֽידַחֲלִנַּ֑נִי וְהַרְהֹרִין֙ עַֽל־ מִשְׁכְּבִ֔י וְחֶזְוֵ֥י רֵאשִׁ֖י יְבַהֲלֻנַּֽנִי׃

passages.text: So I issued a decree that all the wise men of Babylon be brought before me to interpret the dream for me.
passages.sermon:
I am Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon.
I had a troubling dream.
I wanted to know its meaning.
I gave an order.
I commanded all the wise men of Babylon to come before me.
I wanted them to explain my dream to me.
passages.original: וּמִנִּי֙ שִׂ֣ים טְעֵ֔ם לְהַנְעָלָ֣ה קָֽדָמַ֔י לְכֹ֖ל חַכִּימֵ֣י בָבֶ֑ל דִּֽי־ פְשַׁ֥ר חֶלְמָ֖א יְהֽוֹדְעֻנַּֽנִי׃

passages.text: When the magicians, enchanters, astrologers, and diviners came in, I told them the dream, and they could not interpret it for me.
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar had a troubling dream.
He called for the wise men of Babylon.
The magicians came in.
The enchanters came in.
The astrologers came in.
The diviners came in.
I told them my dream.
They could not explain the meaning to me.
passages.original: בֵּאדַ֣יִן עָלֲלִין חַרְטֻמַיָּא֙ אָֽשְׁפַיָּ֔א כַּשְׂדָּיֵא וְגָזְרַיָּ֑א וְחֶלְמָ֗א אָמַ֤ר אֲנָה֙ קֳדָ֣מֵיה֔וֹן וּפִשְׁרֵ֖הּ לָא־ מְהוֹדְעִ֥ין לִֽי׃

passages.text: But at last, into my presence came Daniel (whose name is Belteshazzar after the name of my god, and in whom is the spirit of the holy gods). And I told him the dream: “O Belteshazzar, chief of the magicians, I know that the spirit of the holy gods is in you and that no mystery baffles you. So explain to me the visions I saw in my dream, and their interpretation.
passages.sermon:
Daniel came before me at last.
His Babylonian name is Belteshazzar.
I named him after my god.
The spirit of the holy gods is in him.
I told Daniel my dream.
I said, “Belteshazzar, you are chief of the magicians.
I know the spirit of the holy gods is in you.
No mystery is too hard for you.
Tell me the visions I saw in my dream.
Tell me what they mean.”
passages.original: וְעַ֣ד אָחֳרֵ֡ין עַל֩ קָֽדָמַ֨י דָּנִיֵּ֜אל דִּֽי־ שְׁמֵ֤הּ בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּר֙ כְּשֻׁ֣ם אֱלָהִ֔י וְדִ֛י רֽוּחַ־ אֱלָהִ֥ין קַדִּישִׁ֖ין בֵּ֑הּ וְחֶלְמָ֖א קָֽדָמ֥וֹהִי אַמְרֵֽת׃ בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּר֮ רַ֣ב חַרְטֻמַיָּא֒ דִּ֣י׀ אֲנָ֣ה יִדְעֵ֗ת דִּ֠י ר֣וּחַ אֱלָהִ֤ין קַדִּישִׁין֙ בָּ֔ךְ וְכָל־ רָ֖ז לָא־ אָנֵ֣ס לָ֑ךְ חֶזְוֵ֨י חֶלְמִ֧י דִֽי־ חֲזֵ֛ית וּפִשְׁרֵ֖הּ אֱמַֽר׃

passages.text: In these visions of my mind as I was lying in bed, I saw this come to pass: There was a tree in the midst of the land, and its height was great.
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar had a dream while he was lying in bed.
He saw visions in his mind.
He saw a tree.
The tree stood in the middle of the land.
The tree was very tall.
passages.original: וְחֶזְוֵ֥י רֵאשִׁ֖י עַֽל־ מִשְׁכְּבִ֑י חָזֵ֣ה הֲוֵ֔ית וַאֲל֥וּ אִילָ֛ן בְּג֥וֹא אַרְעָ֖א וְרוּמֵ֥הּ שַׂגִּֽיא׃

passages.text: The tree grew large and strong; its top reached the sky, and it was visible to the ends of the earth.
passages.sermon:
The tree stood in the middle of the land.
The tree grew very large.
The tree became strong.
The top of the tree reached up to the sky.
People could see the tree from every part of the earth.
passages.original: רְבָ֥ה אִֽילָנָ֖א וּתְקִ֑ף וְרוּמֵהּ֙ יִמְטֵ֣א לִשְׁמַיָּ֔א וַחֲזוֹתֵ֖הּ לְס֥וֹף כָּל־ אַרְעָֽא׃

passages.text: Its leaves were beautiful, its fruit was abundant, and upon it was food for all. Under it the beasts of the field found shelter, in its branches the birds of the air nested, and from it every creature was fed.
passages.sermon:
The tree stood in the midst of the land.
Its leaves were beautiful.
Its fruit was abundant.
The tree provided food for all.
The beasts of the field found shelter under the tree.
The birds of the air nested in its branches.
Every creature received food from the tree.
passages.original: עָפְיֵ֤הּ שַׁפִּיר֙ וְאִנְבֵּ֣הּ שַׂגִּ֔יא וּמָז֨וֹן לְכֹ֖לָּא־ בֵ֑הּ תְּחֹת֜וֹהִי תַּטְלֵ֣ל׀ חֵיוַ֣ת בָּרָ֗א וּבְעַנְפ֙וֹהִי֙ יְדֻרוּן צִפֲּרֵ֣י שְׁמַיָּ֔א וּמִנֵּ֖הּ יִתְּזִ֥ין כָּל־ בִּשְׂרָֽא׃

passages.text: As I lay on my bed, I also saw in the visions of my mind a watcher, a holy one, coming down from heaven.
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar had a dream while he lay on his bed.
He saw visions in his mind.
He saw a watcher.
The watcher was a holy one.
The holy one came down from heaven.
passages.original: חָזֵ֥ה הֲוֵ֛ית בְּחֶזְוֵ֥י רֵאשִׁ֖י עַֽל־ מִשְׁכְּבִ֑י וַאֲלוּ֙ עִ֣יר וְקַדִּ֔ישׁ מִן־ שְׁמַיָּ֖א נָחִֽת׃

passages.text: He called out in a loud voice: ‘Cut down the tree and chop off its branches; strip off its leaves and scatter its fruit. Let the beasts flee from under it, and the birds from its branches.
passages.sermon:
A holy messenger came down from heaven.
He called out in a loud voice.
He gave a command about the tree.
He said, "Cut down the tree.
Chop off its branches.
Strip off its leaves.
Scatter its fruit.
Let the beasts run away from under the tree.
Let the birds fly away from its branches."
passages.original: קָרֵ֨א בְחַ֜יִל וְכֵ֣ן אָמַ֗ר גֹּ֤דּוּ אִֽילָנָא֙ וְקַצִּ֣צוּ עַנְפ֔וֹהִי אַתַּ֥רוּ עָפְיֵ֖הּ וּבַדַּ֣רוּ אִנְבֵּ֑הּ תְּנֻ֤ד חֵֽיוְתָא֙ מִן־ תַּחְתּ֔וֹהִי וְצִפְּרַיָּ֖א מִן־ עַנְפֽוֹהִי׃

passages.text: But leave the stump with its roots in the ground, and a band of iron and bronze around it, in the tender grass of the field. Let him be drenched with the dew of heaven and graze with the beasts on the grass of the earth.
passages.sermon:
The watcher is a holy one from heaven.
He gives a command about the tree.
Leave the stump of the tree in the ground.
Keep its roots in the earth.
Put a band of iron and bronze around the stump.
The stump stands in the tender grass of the field.
Let him be drenched with the dew from heaven.
Let him share the grass of the earth with the beasts.
passages.original: בְּרַ֨ם עִקַּ֤ר שָׁרְשׁ֙וֹהִי֙ בְּאַרְעָ֣א שְׁבֻ֔קוּ וּבֶֽאֱסוּר֙ דִּֽי־ פַרְזֶ֣ל וּנְחָ֔שׁ בְּדִתְאָ֖א דִּ֣י בָרָ֑א וּבְטַ֤ל שְׁמַיָּא֙ יִצְטַבַּ֔ע וְעִם־ חֵיוְתָ֥א חֲלָקֵ֖הּ בַּעֲשַׂ֥ב אַרְעָֽא׃

passages.text: Let his mind be changed from that of a man, and let him be given the mind of a beast till seven times pass him by.
passages.sermon:
God sent a message to King Nebuchadnezzar in a dream.
God decided to change Nebuchadnezzar’s mind.
God would take away his human mind.
God would give him the mind of a beast.
Nebuchadnezzar would live like this for seven periods of time.
God would do this to show His power over kings.
passages.original: לִבְבֵהּ֙ מִן־ אֱנוֹשָׁא יְשַׁנּ֔וֹן וּלְבַ֥ב חֵיוָ֖ה יִתְיְהִ֣ב לֵ֑הּ וְשִׁבְעָ֥ה עִדָּנִ֖ין יַחְלְפ֥וּן עֲלֽוֹהִי׃

passages.text: This decision is the decree of the watchers, the verdict declared by the holy ones, so that the living will know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of mankind and gives it to whom He wishes, setting over it the lowliest of men.’
passages.sermon:
The watchers are holy angels.
They have made a decree.
The holy ones have given a verdict.
This decision comes from them.
God is the Most High.
God rules over the kingdom of mankind.
God gives the kingdom to anyone He wishes.
God can set even the lowliest of men over the kingdom.
God wants the living to know this truth.
passages.original: בִּגְזֵרַ֤ת עִירִין֙ פִּתְגָמָ֔א וּמֵאמַ֥ר קַדִּישִׁ֖ין שְׁאֵֽלְתָ֑א עַד־ דִּבְרַ֡ת דִּ֣י יִנְדְּע֣וּן חַ֠יַּיָּא דִּֽי־ שַׁלִּ֨יט עִלָּיָא בְּמַלְכ֣וּת אֱנוֹשָׁא וּלְמַן־ דִּ֤י יִצְבֵּא֙ יִתְּנִנַּ֔הּ וּשְׁפַ֥ל אֲנָשִׁ֖ים יְקִ֥ים עֲלַיַּהּ׃

passages.text: This is the dream that I, King Nebuchadnezzar, saw. Now, Belteshazzar, tell me the interpretation, because none of the wise men of my kingdom can interpret it for me. But you are able, because the spirit of the holy gods is in you.”
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar had a dream.
He saw this dream himself.
He was the ruler of Babylon.
He spoke to Belteshazzar.
Belteshazzar was also called Daniel.
Nebuchadnezzar said, “This is the dream I saw.”
He asked Belteshazzar to explain the dream.
He said, “None of the wise men in my kingdom can interpret it for me.”
He said, “You can explain it.”
He said, “The spirit of the holy gods is in you.”
passages.original: דְּנָה֙ חֶלְמָ֣א חֲזֵ֔ית אֲנָ֖ה מַלְכָּ֣א נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֑ר וְאַנְתָּה בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּ֜ר פִּשְׁרֵ֣א׀ אֱמַ֗ר כָּל־ קֳבֵל֙ דִּ֣י׀ כָּל־ חַכִּימֵ֣י מַלְכוּתִ֗י לָֽא־ יָכְלִ֤ין פִּשְׁרָא֙ לְהוֹדָ֣עֻתַ֔נִי וְאַנְתָּה כָּהֵ֔ל דִּ֛י רֽוּחַ־ אֱלָהִ֥ין קַדִּישִׁ֖ין בָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: For a time, Daniel, who was also known as Belteshazzar, was perplexed, and his thoughts alarmed him. So the king said, “Belteshazzar, do not let the dream or its interpretation alarm you.” “My lord,” replied Belteshazzar, “may the dream apply to those who hate you, and its interpretation to your enemies!
passages.sermon:
Daniel was also called Belteshazzar.
Daniel heard the dream from King Nebuchadnezzar.
Daniel was perplexed for a while.
Daniel’s thoughts alarmed him.
King Nebuchadnezzar noticed Daniel’s distress.
The king spoke to Daniel.
The king said, “Belteshazzar, do not let the dream or its interpretation alarm you.”
Belteshazzar answered the king.
Belteshazzar said, “My lord, may the dream be for those who hate you.”
Belteshazzar said, “May its interpretation be for your enemies.”
passages.original: אֱדַ֨יִן דָּֽנִיֵּ֜אל דִּֽי־ שְׁמֵ֣הּ בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּ֗ר אֶשְׁתּוֹמַם֙ כְּשָׁעָ֣ה חֲדָ֔ה וְרַעְיֹנֹ֖הִי יְבַהֲלֻנֵּ֑הּ עָנֵ֨ה מַלְכָּ֜א וְאָמַ֗ר בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּר֙ חֶלְמָ֤א וּפִשְׁרֵא֙ אַֽל־ יְבַהֲלָ֔ךְ עָנֵ֤ה בֵלְטְשַׁאצַּר֙ וְאָמַ֔ר מָרְאִי חֶלְמָ֥א לְשָׂנְאַיִךְ וּפִשְׁרֵ֥הּ לְעָרַיִךְ׃

passages.text: The tree you saw that grew large and strong, whose top reached the sky and was visible to all the earth, whose foliage was beautiful and whose fruit was abundant, providing food for all, under which the beasts of the field lived, and in whose branches the birds of the air nested— you, O king, are that tree! For you have become great and strong; your greatness has grown to reach the sky, and your dominion extends to the ends of the earth.
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar had a dream about a tree.
The tree grew large and strong.
The top of the tree reached the sky.
Everyone on earth could see the tree.
The tree had beautiful leaves.
The tree had much fruit.
The tree gave food to all.
Wild animals lived under the tree.
Birds made their nests in its branches.
Daniel spoke to the king.
Daniel said, “You, O king, are that tree.”
The king had become great and strong.
The king’s greatness reached to the sky.
The king’s rule extended to the ends of the earth.
passages.original: אִֽילָנָא֙ דִּ֣י חֲזַ֔יְתָ דִּ֥י רְבָ֖ה וּתְקִ֑ף וְרוּמֵהּ֙ יִמְטֵ֣א לִשְׁמַיָּ֔א וַחֲזוֹתֵ֖הּ לְכָל־ אַרְעָֽא׃ וְעָפְיֵ֤הּ שַׁפִּיר֙ וְאִנְבֵּ֣הּ שַׂגִּ֔יא וּמָז֨וֹן לְכֹ֖לָּא־ בֵ֑הּ תְּחֹת֗וֹהִי תְּדוּר֙ חֵיוַ֣ת בָּרָ֔א וּבְעַנְפ֕וֹהִי יִשְׁכְּנָ֖ן צִפֲּרֵ֥י שְׁמַיָּֽא׃ אַנְתָּה ה֣וּא מַלְכָּ֔א דִּ֥י רְבַ֖ית וּתְקֵ֑פְתְּ וּרְבוּתָ֤ךְ רְבָת֙ וּמְטָ֣ת לִשְׁמַיָּ֔א וְשָׁלְטָנָ֖ךְ לְס֥וֹף אַרְעָֽא׃

passages.text: And you, O king, saw a watcher, a holy one, coming down from heaven and saying: ‘Cut down the tree and destroy it, but leave the stump with its roots in the ground, and a band of iron and bronze around it, in the tender grass of the field. Let him be drenched with the dew of heaven, and graze with the beasts of the field till seven times pass him by.’
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar had a dream.
He saw a watcher.
The watcher was a holy one.
The holy one came down from heaven.
The holy one gave a command.
He said, “Cut down the tree.
Destroy the tree.
But leave the stump with its roots in the ground.
Put a band of iron and bronze around the stump.
Let the stump remain in the tender grass of the field.
Let him be drenched with the dew of heaven.
Let him live with the beasts of the field.
This will last until seven times pass over him.”
passages.original: וְדִ֣י חֲזָ֣ה מַלְכָּ֡א עִ֣יר וְקַדִּ֣ישׁ נָחִ֣ת׀ מִן־ שְׁמַיָּ֡א וְאָמַר֩ גֹּ֨דּוּ אִֽילָנָ֜א וְחַבְּל֗וּהִי בְּרַ֨ם עִקַּ֤ר שָׁרְשׁ֙וֹהִי֙ בְּאַרְעָ֣א שְׁבֻ֔קוּ וּבֶאֱסוּר֙ דִּֽי־ פַרְזֶ֣ל וּנְחָ֔שׁ בְּדִתְאָ֖א דִּ֣י בָרָ֑א וּבְטַ֧ל שְׁמַיָּ֣א יִצְטַבַּ֗ע וְעִם־ חֵיוַ֤ת בָּרָא֙ חֲלָקֵ֔הּ עַ֛ד דִּֽי־ שִׁבְעָ֥ה עִדָּנִ֖ין יַחְלְפ֥וּן עֲלֽוֹהִי׃

passages.text: This is the interpretation, O king, and this is the decree that the Most High has issued against my lord the king: You will be driven away from mankind, and your dwelling will be with the beasts of the field. You will feed on grass like an ox and be drenched with the dew of heaven, and seven times shall pass you by, until you acknowledge that the Most High rules over the kingdom of mankind and gives it to whom He wishes.
passages.sermon:
O king, I will explain the meaning to you.
The Most High God has made a decree against you, my lord the king.
You will be driven away from other people.
You will live with the wild animals of the field.
You will eat grass like an ox.
The dew from heaven will drench you.
Seven periods of time will pass over you.
This will continue until you understand something important.
You must know that the Most High God rules over the kingdoms of men.
He gives these kingdoms to anyone He chooses.
passages.original: דְּנָ֥ה פִשְׁרָ֖א מַלְכָּ֑א וּגְזֵרַ֤ת עִלָּיָא הִ֔יא דִּ֥י מְטָ֖ת עַל־ מַרְאִי מַלְכָּֽא׃ וְלָ֣ךְ טָֽרְדִ֣ין מִן־ אֲנָשָׁ֡א וְעִם־ חֵיוַ֣ת בָּרָא֩ לֶהֱוֵ֨ה מְדֹרָ֜ךְ וְעִשְׂבָּ֥א כְתוֹרִ֣ין׀ לָ֣ךְ יְטַֽעֲמ֗וּן וּמִטַּ֤ל שְׁמַיָּא֙ לָ֣ךְ מְצַבְּעִ֔ין וְשִׁבְעָ֥ה עִדָּנִ֖ין יַחְלְפ֣וּן עֲלָ֑יךְ עַ֣ד דִּֽי־ תִנְדַּ֗ע דִּֽי־ שַׁלִּ֤יט עִלָּיאָ֙ בְּמַלְכ֣וּת אֲנָשָׁ֔א וּלְמַן־ דִּ֥י יִצְבֵּ֖א יִתְּנִנַּֽהּ׃

passages.text: As for the command to leave the stump of the tree with its roots, your kingdom will be restored to you as soon as you acknowledge that Heaven rules.
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar had a dream.
A holy messenger from God spoke in the dream.
The messenger commanded that the tree’s stump and roots must remain in the ground.
This tree represents your kingdom, O king.
Your kingdom will not be destroyed forever.
Your kingdom will remain for you.
This will happen after you understand one thing.
You must know that Heaven rules over all.
When you acknowledge that God in Heaven is the true ruler, your kingdom will be restored to you.
passages.original: וְדִ֣י אֲמַ֗רוּ לְמִשְׁבַּ֞ק עִקַּ֤ר שָׁרְשׁ֙וֹהִי֙ דִּ֣י אִֽילָנָ֔א מַלְכוּתָ֖ךְ לָ֣ךְ קַיָּמָ֑ה מִן־ דִּ֣י תִנְדַּ֔ע דִּ֥י שַׁלִּטִ֖ן שְׁמַיָּֽא׃

passages.text: Therefore, may my advice be pleasing to you, O king. Break away from your sins by doing what is right, and from your iniquities by showing mercy to the oppressed. Perhaps there will be an extension of your prosperity.”
passages.sermon:
Daniel spoke to King Nebuchadnezzar.
Daniel gave advice to the king.
Daniel said, "O king, please accept my advice."
Daniel told the king to turn away from his sins.
Daniel said, "Do what is right."
Daniel told the king to turn away from his iniquities.
Daniel said, "Show mercy to people who are oppressed."
Daniel said, "If you do this, your prosperity may continue."
passages.original: לָהֵ֣ן מַלְכָּ֗א מִלְכִּי֙ יִשְׁפַּ֣ר עֲלַיִךְ וַחֲטָיָךְ בְּצִדְקָ֣ה פְרֻ֔ק וַעֲוָיָתָ֖ךְ בְּמִחַ֣ן עֲנָ֑יִן הֵ֛ן תֶּהֱוֵ֥א אַרְכָ֖ה לִשְׁלֵוְתָֽךְ׃

passages.text: All this happened to King Nebuchadnezzar.
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar ruled Babylon.
God warned King Nebuchadnezzar through a dream and a message.
God said that Nebuchadnezzar would lose his kingdom.
God said this would happen until Nebuchadnezzar learned that God rules over all.
Everything God said came true for King Nebuchadnezzar.
passages.original: כֹּ֣לָּא מְּטָ֔א עַל־ נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֖ר מַלְכָּֽא׃פ

passages.text: Twelve months later, as he was walking on the roof of the royal palace of Babylon, the king exclaimed, “Is this not Babylon the Great, which I myself have built by the might of my power as a royal residence and for the glory of my majesty?”
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar ruled Babylon.
He was a powerful and proud king.
Twelve months passed.
Nebuchadnezzar walked on the roof of his royal palace in Babylon.
He looked at the city.
He spoke with pride.
He said, “This is Babylon the Great.”
He said, “I built this city.”
He said, “I built it as a royal home.”
He said, “I built it by my own strength.”
He said, “I built it for the glory of my majesty.”
passages.original: לִקְצָ֥ת יַרְחִ֖ין תְּרֵֽי־ עֲשַׂ֑ר עַל־ הֵיכַ֧ל מַלְכוּתָ֛א דִּ֥י בָבֶ֖ל מְהַלֵּ֥ךְ הֲוָֽה׃ עָנֵ֤ה מַלְכָּא֙ וְאָמַ֔ר הֲלָ֥א דָא־ הִ֖יא בָּבֶ֣ל רַבְּתָ֑א דִּֽי־ אֲנָ֤ה בֱנַיְתַהּ֙ לְבֵ֣ית מַלְכ֔וּ בִּתְקַ֥ף חִסְנִ֖י וְלִיקָ֥ר הַדְרִֽי׃

passages.text: While the words were still in the king’s mouth, a voice came from heaven: “It is decreed to you, King Nebuchadnezzar, that the kingdom has departed from you.
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar was the ruler of Babylon.
He spoke proud words about his kingdom.
While King Nebuchadnezzar was still speaking, a voice came from heaven.
The voice spoke directly to King Nebuchadnezzar.
The voice said, “King Nebuchadnezzar, this message is for you.
The kingdom has been taken away from you.”
passages.original: ע֗וֹד מִלְּתָא֙ בְּפֻ֣ם מַלְכָּ֔א קָ֖ל מִן־ שְׁמַיָּ֣א נְפַ֑ל לָ֤ךְ אָֽמְרִין֙ נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֣ר מַלְכָּ֔א מַלְכוּתָ֖ה עֲדָ֥ת מִנָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: You will be driven away from mankind to live with the beasts of the field, and you will feed on grass like an ox. And seven times will pass you by, until you acknowledge that the Most High rules over the kingdom of mankind and gives it to whom He wishes.”
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar, you will be separated from other people.
You will live with the wild animals of the field.
You will eat grass as an ox eats grass.
Seven periods of time will pass over you.
This will continue until you understand something important.
The Most High God rules over the kingdoms of men.
God gives these kingdoms to anyone He chooses.
passages.original: וּמִן־ אֲנָשָׁא֩ לָ֨ךְ טָֽרְדִ֜ין וְֽעִם־ חֵיוַ֧ת בָּרָ֣א מְדֹרָ֗ךְ עִשְׂבָּ֤א כְתוֹרִין֙ לָ֣ךְ יְטַעֲמ֔וּן וְשִׁבְעָ֥ה עִדָּנִ֖ין יַחְלְפ֣וּן עִלַיִךְ עַ֣ד דִּֽי־ תִנְדַּ֗ע דִּֽי־ שַׁלִּ֤יט עִלָּיאָ֙ בְּמַלְכ֣וּת אֲנָשָׁ֔א וּלְמַן־ דִּ֥י יִצְבֵּ֖א יִתְּנִנַּֽהּ׃

passages.text: At that moment the sentence against Nebuchadnezzar was fulfilled. He was driven away from mankind. He ate grass like an ox, and his body was drenched with the dew of heaven, until his hair grew like the feathers of an eagle and his nails like the claws of a bird.
passages.sermon:
Nebuchadnezzar was the king of Babylon.
God spoke a sentence against Nebuchadnezzar.
At that moment, the sentence was fulfilled.
People drove Nebuchadnezzar away from other men.
Nebuchadnezzar lived apart from mankind.
He ate grass like an ox.
The dew from heaven drenched his body.
His hair grew long like the feathers of an eagle.
His nails became like the claws of a bird.
passages.original: בַּהּ־ שַׁעֲתָ֗א מִלְּתָא֮ סָ֣פַת עַל־ נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר֒ וּמִן־ אֲנָשָׁ֣א טְרִ֔יד וְעִשְׂבָּ֤א כְתוֹרִין֙ יֵאכֻ֔ל וּמִטַּ֥ל שְׁמַיָּ֖א גִּשְׁמֵ֣הּ יִצְטַבַּ֑ע עַ֣ד דִּ֥י שַׂעְרֵ֛הּ כְּנִשְׁרִ֥ין רְבָ֖ה וְטִפְר֥וֹהִי כְצִפְּרִֽין׃

passages.text: But at the end of those days I, Nebuchadnezzar, looked up to heaven, and my sanity was restored to me. Then I praised the Most High, and I honored and glorified Him who lives forever: “For His dominion is an everlasting dominion, and His kingdom endures from generation to generation.
passages.sermon:
Nebuchadnezzar was the king of Babylon.
He lost his sanity and lived away from people.
At the end of those days, I, Nebuchadnezzar, looked up to heaven.
My sanity returned to me.
I praised the Most High God.
I honored and glorified God who lives forever.
God’s rule lasts forever.
His kingdom continues through every generation.
passages.original: וְלִקְצָ֣ת יֽוֹמַיָּה֩ אֲנָ֨ה נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֜ר עַיְנַ֣י׀ לִשְׁמַיָּ֣א נִטְלֵ֗ת וּמַנְדְּעִי֙ עֲלַ֣י יְת֔וּב וּלְעִלָּיָא בָּרְכֵ֔ת וּלְחַ֥י עָלְמָ֖א שַׁבְּחֵ֣ת וְהַדְּרֵ֑ת דִּ֤י שָׁלְטָנֵהּ֙ שָׁלְטָ֣ן עָלַ֔ם וּמַלְכוּתֵ֖הּ עִם־ דָּ֥ר וְדָֽר׃

passages.text: All the peoples of the earth are counted as nothing, and He does as He pleases with the army of heaven and the peoples of the earth. There is no one who can restrain His hand or say to Him, ‘What have You done?’ ”
passages.sermon:
God rules over all people on earth.
God considers all people as nothing before Him.
God acts as He wishes with the armies of heaven.
God acts as He wishes with the people of earth.
No one can stop God’s hand.
No one can question God or say, “What have You done?”
passages.original: וְכָל־ דָּאֲרֵי אַרְעָא֙ כְּלָ֣ה חֲשִׁיבִ֔ין וּֽכְמִצְבְּיֵ֗הּ עָבֵד֙ בְּחֵ֣יל שְׁמַיָּ֔א וְדָאֲרֵי אַרְעָ֑א וְלָ֤א אִיתַי֙ דִּֽי־ יְמַחֵ֣א בִידֵ֔הּ וְיֵ֥אמַר לֵ֖הּ מָ֥ה עֲבַֽדְתְּ׃

passages.text: At the same time my sanity was restored, my honor and splendor returned to me for the glory of my kingdom. My advisers and nobles sought me out, and I was restored to my throne, and surpassing greatness was added to me.
passages.sermon:
Nebuchadnezzar was the king of Babylon.
God had taken away Nebuchadnezzar’s sanity because of his pride.
At the end of that time, God restored Nebuchadnezzar’s sanity.
God gave Nebuchadnezzar back his understanding.
Nebuchadnezzar’s honor returned to him.
His splendor came back for the glory of his kingdom.
His advisers came to him again.
His nobles looked for him.
Nebuchadnezzar was restored to his throne.
God gave Nebuchadnezzar even greater greatness than before.
passages.original: בֵּהּ־ זִמְנָ֞א מַנְדְּעִ֣י׀ יְת֣וּב עֲלַ֗י וְלִיקַ֨ר מַלְכוּתִ֜י הַדְרִ֤י וְזִוִי֙ יְת֣וּב עֲלַ֔י וְלִ֕י הַדָּֽבְרַ֥י וְרַבְרְבָנַ֖י יְבַע֑וֹן וְעַל־ מַלְכוּתִ֣י הָתְקְנַ֔ת וּרְב֥וּ יַתִּירָ֖ה ה֥וּסְפַת לִֽי׃

passages.text: Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and exalt and glorify the King of heaven, for all His works are true and all His ways are just. And He is able to humble those who walk in pride.
passages.sermon:
I am Nebuchadnezzar.
I praise the King of heaven.
I exalt the King of heaven.
I glorify the King of heaven.
All the works of the King of heaven are true.
All the ways of the King of heaven are just.
The King of heaven can humble anyone who walks in pride.
passages.original: כְּעַ֞ן אֲנָ֣ה נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֗ר מְשַׁבַּ֨ח וּמְרוֹמֵ֤ם וּמְהַדַּר֙ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ שְׁמַיָּ֔א דִּ֤י כָל־ מַעֲבָד֙וֹהִי֙ קְשֹׁ֔ט וְאֹרְחָתֵ֖הּ דִּ֑ין וְדִי֙ מַהְלְכִ֣ין בְּגֵוָ֔ה יָכִ֖ל לְהַשְׁפָּלָֽה׃פ
